title: L-PRF augmented dural closure in elective intracranial surgery
summary: Surgical procedures performed on the brain or pituitary require opening of the dura mater (a tough, outer layer of tissue that protects the brain and encloses cerebrospinal fluid, CSF). The dura mater is then closed at the end of surgery either by sutering or with the help of synthetic materials. Water-tight closure of the dura mater is important in protecting patients from future complications including wound healing disorders, meningitis and CSF leaks. However, in some cases, water-tight closure is not possible (for example when the dura mater is to thin to suture or was damaged due to tumor growth). To date, several synthetic materials and suture techniques are available to achieve dural closure. In this study  the use of an autologous (from the patient's own body) material will be examined in its efficiency for closure of the dura mater. This material is called L-PRF (Leukocyte and Platelette rich Fibrinogen), which is extracted from a patients own blood by centrifugation. With this study, the number of postoperative CSF leaks ocurring following closure of the dura mater using suturing as well as L-PRF alone or suturing with L-PRF combined with conventional synthetic materials compared to conventional suturing with synthetic materials alone will be examined.

interventions.name: Dural Closure augmented  with L-PRF alone
Conventional dural closure with synthetic materials and without augmentation using L-PRF

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Elective resection of sellar tumors (pituitary adenomas), elective craniotomy and resction of supratentorial lesions, elective craniotomy and resection of infratentorial lesions, age > 18 years
Exclusion criteria:
Age <18 years, preoperative signs of boney destruction of the skull or skull base, patients undergoing repeat surgical intervention, obvious intraoperative CSF fistula among patients undergoing transsphenoidal surgery.
